title: The ring of integers is excellent
statement: The commutative ring $\mathbf Z$ is excellent [def-exc-excellent-ring].

source.place: Proposition 15.53.3, Tag 07QW, proposition-ubiquity-excellent, item (3), lines 13385–13412: the integer-ring seed, not just preservation of excellence.

proof.text: First check Noetherianity and regularity of $\mathbf Z$. By [lem-weil-pbc-z-localizations-dvr] it is Noetherian, its primes are $(0)$ and $(p)$ for rational primes $p$, its localization at $(0)$ is $\mathbf Q$, and its localization at $(p)$ is a one-dimensional Noetherian local ring with principal maximal ideal. The field case is regular local by [lem-weil-pbc-field-regular-ring]. In the other case one generator generates the maximal ideal and the dimension is one, which is exactly the regular-local condition of [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Thus every prime localization is regular local, so $\mathbf Z$ is regular.

source.place: Tag 07QW, proposition-ubiquity-excellent, proof: regular rings are universally catenary; verify regularity of the integer-ring seed.

proof.text: The G-ring condition for $\mathbf Z$ is precisely the statement of [lem-weil-pbc-z-g-ring]. Apply it to obtain the geometrically regular formal fibres required by excellence.

source.place: Tag 07QW, proposition-ubiquity-excellent, proof referring to Tag 07PX, proposition-ubiquity-G-ring, item (3).

proof.text: For the J-2 criterion, first take the prime $(0)$. Its residue field is $\mathbf Q$ by [lem-weil-pbc-z-localizations-dvr]. A finite purely inseparable extension $L/\mathbf Q$ is trivial by the characteristic-zero clause of [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension]. Identify $L$ with the image of $\mathbf Q$ under its structure map and take $B$ to be the image of $\mathbf Z$ in $L$. This is a $\mathbf Z$-subalgebra generated by $1$ as a module, and all elements of $L$ are fractions of elements of $B$. Step 1 gives regularity of all prime localizations of $B\cong\mathbf Z$. Thus the whole $\operatorname{Spec}B$ is a nonempty regular open subset, nonempty because $(0)$ is prime.

source.place: Tag 07PJ, proposition-ubiquity-J-2, proof for case (3): verify condition (4) of Tag 07PC, lemma-J-2, at the zero prime.

proof.text: Now take a nonzero prime $(p)$, as classified in [lem-weil-pbc-z-localizations-dvr]. The residue field $\kappa((p))=\mathbf Z_{(p)}/p\mathbf Z_{(p)}$, the maximal ideal being $(p)\mathbf Z_{(p)}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-z-localizations-dvr], is $\mathbf F_p=\mathbf Z/p\mathbf Z$. Indeed, for an integer $s$ not divisible by $p$, Bezout gives $u,v$ with $us+vp=1$; hence $a/s-au=avp/s\in p\mathbf Z_{(p)}$ for every integer $a$, so $\mathbf Z\to\kappa((p))$ is surjective, and its kernel is a proper ideal containing $p$, hence equal to $p\mathbf Z$ since $p$ is prime. In particular every element of $\kappa((p))$ is an integer multiple of $1$, and $p=0$ in it. Let $L/\mathbf F_p$ be finite purely inseparable. By [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension], for $x\in L$ there are $n\ge0$ and $a\in\mathbf F_p$ with $x^{p^n}=a$. In characteristic $p$, the binomial expansion gives $(z+w)^p=z^p+w^p$ since $p$ divides the intermediate binomial coefficients. It follows by iteration that the $p^n$-power map is additive, and it fixes $1$, hence every integer multiple of $1$, hence every $a\in\mathbf F_p$. Consequently $(x-a)^{p^n}=0$ and $x=a$, since $L$ is a field. Thus the extension is trivial. Take $B$ to be the image of $\mathbf F_p$ in $L$. It is the image of $\mathbf Z$, hence finite as a $\mathbf Z$-module generated by $1$; its fraction field is $L=B$. By [lem-weil-pbc-field-regular-ring], its whole spectrum is regular, and it is nonempty because the zero ideal of a field is prime. These are the required witnesses at every nonzero prime.

source.place: Tag 07PJ, proposition-ubiquity-J-2, proof for case (3): verify condition (4) of Tag 07PC, lemma-J-2, at the nonzero primes.

proof.text: Apply [lem-exc-j2-residue-field-criterion] with $R=\mathbf Z$. Noetherianity is Step 1. For every prime and every finite purely inseparable residue-field extension, Steps 3 and 4 give a finite $\mathbf Z$-subalgebra of that extension with the specified fraction field and a nonempty regular open. The criterion therefore makes the regular locus open in every finite type $\mathbf Z$-algebra; this is the J-2 condition.

source.place: Tag 07PC, lemma-J-2, implication (4) implies (1), as used in Tag 07PJ, proposition-ubiquity-J-2.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-regular-ring-universally-catenary] to $R=\mathbf Z$, using the Noetherianity and prime-local regularity proved in Step 1. This gives universal catenarity, including the equal-length saturated-chain condition in every finite type $\mathbf Z$-algebra.

source.place: Tag 00NM, lemma-CM-ring-catenary, regular-ring consequence; Tag 00NQ, lemma-regular-ring-CM.

proof.text: By [def-exc-excellent-ring], Noetherianity (Step 1), the G-ring condition (Step 2), and J-2 (Step 5) make $\mathbf Z$ quasi-excellent. Universal catenarity (Step 6) then makes it excellent, exactly as asserted.

source.place: Tag 07QT, definition-excellent, and Tag 07QW, proposition-ubiquity-excellent, item (3).

One repair in Step 4: it said the residue field is Z/pZ but proved only that Z/pZ is a field. The argument needs every element of the residue field to be an integer multiple of 1, so that Frobenius fixes a. I added the surjectivity argument (Bezout: a/s - au in pZ_(p)) and the kernel argument (kernel = pZ). The uses are unchanged and the step stays elementary; the corrected item is in fixes/dag/nodes/sec-trace-formula/. The new node lem-trf-regular-ring-universally-catenary is true (regular local implies CM by 00NQ; Noetherian CM implies universally catenary by 00NM). I tested it on fields, Z, DVRs, the zero ring, finite products of fields and Nagata's infinite-dimensional regular ring. It is statement-only and self-contained, cites a definition node for every notion, matches the definition's catenary clause, and records all three kinds of Mathlib search; my own rg of Mathlib for catenar/CohenMacaulay finds nothing. Its blueprint from/via and created fields are correct. It duplicates no DAG node: the existing catenary nodes assume universal catenarity, cover only fields, or are local CM chain-length lemmas. It is strictly more general than the item and not a clause of it.
